did_you_know.text: Did you know? In chapter 3, God speaks to Jonah a second time and renews his mission to Nineveh after the first mission was not carried out.
Did you know? Jonah is commanded not only to go to Nineveh, but also to proclaim to it exactly the words God will tell him.
Did you know? Jonah gets up and goes to Nineveh as the Lord commanded. The text describes Nineveh as “a great city to God” and as a city that takes three days to cross.
Did you know? Jonah begins to enter the city, traveling for one day, and proclaims: “Forty more days, and Nineveh will be overthrown.”
Did you know? The people of Nineveh believe in God, proclaim a fast, and put on sackcloth—from the greatest to the least.
Did you know? The king of Nineveh also responds immediately: he rises from his throne, removes his robe, covers himself with sackcloth, and sits in ashes.
Did you know? The king’s decree, issued with his nobles, includes a complete fast: not only the people, but also the cattle and sheep are forbidden to eat, drink, or graze.
Did you know? The fast in Nineveh is not presented as merely an outward act: the people are called to turn from their evil ways and from the violence in their hands, and to call on God urgently.
Did you know? The people of Nineveh do not assume that deliverance is guaranteed; they say, “Who knows?” Perhaps God will turn from his fierce anger, and they will not perish.
Did you know? When God sees the people of Nineveh’s actions and that they have turned from their evil ways, he does not bring upon them the disaster he had spoken of.
